files.lesson.md: --- order: 12 unit: area node: AC9M8M01 n1 title: Composite shapes summary: "A composite shape is made of shapes you know. Cut it into pieces and add their areas, or see it as a big rectangle with pieces taken away; the area is the same either way. The perimeter is the distance round the outside." language: maths voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } hook: "An L-shaped bedroom, a house front with a pointed roof, a photo frame: none is a single rectangle, but each is easy once you cut it up." connection: l-shaped-floor app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-board" 8303 url: http://127.0.0.1:8303/index.html readySelector: "#gsum" layout: full explainPicture: { ref: shapes.yml#explain-pic, caption: "A U-shape: the 12 m by 9 m rectangle is 108 m², and the gap is 4 m by 5 m, so the area is 108 − 20 = 88 m²." } explainClip: query: { code: "@shapes.yml#explain", fresh: 1, id: explain } caption: "Two ways, one area" say: "Cut it up, or take a piece away. The area is the same." clip: - caption: { text: "An L-shaped room. Cut it up and down into two rectangles.", say: "Cut the L into two rectangles." } - click: Cut up and down - expect: { selector: "#gsum", contains: "18 + 15 = 33" } - wait: 1400 - caption: { text: "Or: a big rectangle with a corner taken away.", say: "Or see a big rectangle, with a corner taken away." } - click: Take away from a rectangle - expect: { selector: "#gsum", contains: "= 33" } - wait: 1600 --- A **composite shape** is made of simple shapes joined together. ## Predict: an L-shaped room ```step stage: predict insight: "Committing to an area for an L-shape shows whether they split it or multiply the two outside lengths." check: type: predict q: "An L-shaped room is 8 m wide and 6 m tall, with a 5 m by 3 m corner missing. What is its area?" options: ["33 m²", "48 m²", "28 m²", "18 m²"] actual: "33 m². The whole 8 by 6 rectangle is 48 m², and the missing corner is 15 m²: 48 − 15 = 33. (28 is the perimeter, in metres.)" ``` Sketch it first, then decide how you would find the area. ## Run: cut it up ```step stage: run insight: "Trying each way of cutting the same shape shows that every valid split, and take-away, gives the same area." try: { playground: board, starter: "shapes.yml#run", height: 600 } check: { type: board, text: "Try a cut, then the take-away. Do they all give the same area? Was your prediction right?", when: "k > 0 and A = 33", explain: "18 + 15, 24 + 9 and 48 − 15 all make 33 m²." } ``` Each button shows a different way to see the same shape. Here's how to find the area of a shape like that: 1. **Cut** it into rectangles, triangles or other shapes you know, find each area and **add** them; or 2. see it as a **big rectangle** and **take away** the pieces that are missing. Read every length you need from the diagram: a missing side is often the difference of two others. The **perimeter** is the total length round the outside, in units of length (m), not area (m²). ## Investigate: lengths and pieces ```step stage: investigate insight: "Missing lengths come from differences of others; each piece needs its own height (Ella uses the whole height twice); every method agrees." tasks: - check: type: answer q: "The L-shape is 8 m along the bottom and 3 m along the top. How long is the step across in the middle?" answer: "5" feedback: - ["11", "The top and the step together make the bottom: 8 − 3."] explain: "The bottom (8 m) = the top (3 m) + the step: 8 − 3 = 5 m." - check: type: bug code: "working.txt#ella" text: "Ella finds the area of the L-shape. Click the line where her working goes wrong." answer: 4 fault: logic misconception: composite-wrong-height explain: "Line 4: the right piece is only 3 m tall, not 6 m. 5 × 3 = 15, so the total is 18 + 15 = 33 m²." - check: type: question q: "Ali cuts the L across, Bea cuts it up and down, and Cal takes a corner away from a rectangle. Who gets the right area?" options: ["All three, if each uses the right lengths", "Only Cal", "Only Ali and Bea", "None: you must use a formula for L-shapes"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "Cutting gives the same area too.", "Taking away gives the same area too.", "There is no special formula: an L is two rectangles."] explain: "The area does not depend on how you cut it, only on using each piece's own lengths." ``` ### Missing lengths Here is the routine. ```worked \text{an L } 10 \text{ m by } 7 \text{ m, a } 6 \times 4 \text{ corner missing} :: A different L, as an example. \text{pieces: } 4 \times 7 \text{ and } 6 \times 3 :: Cut into shapes you know, with each piece's own lengths. 28 + 18 = 46\ \text{m}^2 :: Add the pieces. 10 \times 7 - 6 \times 4 = 70 - 24 = 46\ \text{m}^2 :: Or: the big rectangle, take away the missing corner. 10 + 3 + 6 + 4 + 4 + 7 = 34\ \text{m} :: The perimeter adds every side, in metres. ``` Now find the step. ### Find the mistake Read Ella's working. How tall is each piece? ### Three ways ## Modify: other shapes ```step stage: modify insight: "A U-shape is quickest by taking away, a house needs a triangle, and the perimeter needs missing sides first; units separate area from length." try: { playground: board, starter: "shapes.yml#u-shape", height: 600 } tasks: - starter: "shapes.yml#u-shape" hint: ["The rectangle around the U is 10 m by 8 m.", "The gap is 4 m wide and 5 m deep."] check: { type: board, text: "Find the area of the U-shape by taking away from a rectangle.", when: "k = 3 and A = 60", explain: "10 × 8 − 4 × 5 = 80 − 20 = 60 m²." } - starter: "shapes.yml#house" hint: ["Cut where the roof meets the walls.", "The roof is a triangle: half of base times height."] check: { type: board, text: "The front of a house: walls 4 m tall, the roof's top 7 m up. Cut it into a rectangle and a triangle.", when: "k = 1 and n = 2", explain: "Rectangle 8 × 4 = 32, triangle ½ × 8 × 3 = 12: 44 m²." } - starter: "shapes.yml#hidden" check: type: number q: "Two sides of the L are marked ?. Work them out, then find the perimeter in metres." answer: 28 tolerance: 0 explain: "The ? sides are 8 − 3 = 5 m and 6 − 3 = 3 m. Perimeter: 8 + 3 + 5 + 3 + 3 + 6 = 28 m." - check: type: question q: "A garden has an area of 33 and a perimeter of 28. Which units are right?" options: ["33 m² and 28 m", "33 m and 28 m²", "33 m² and 28 m²", "33 m and 28 m"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "Area counts squares; perimeter is a length.", "A perimeter is a length, not an area.", "An area counts squares, so it needs m²."] explain: "Area is in square units (m²); perimeter is a length (m)." ``` ### Take away ### A house ### Missing sides ### Units ## Practise: composite shapes ```step stage: practise insight: "Adding a triangle, taking away a frame and a perimeter shortcut, mixed; using the whole height for a piece is the planted slip; the triangle review keeps half base times height fresh." tasks: - check: type: number q: "A shape is a rectangle 10 cm by 4 cm with a triangle on top (base 10 cm, height 3 cm). What is its area in cm²?" answer: 55 tolerance: 0 explain: "10 × 4 + ½ × 10 × 3 = 40 + 15 = 55 cm²." - check: type: number q: "A photo frame is 30 cm by 20 cm on the outside, with a 24 cm by 14 cm hole for the photo. What is the frame's area in cm²?" answer: 264 tolerance: 0 explain: "30 × 20 − 24 × 14 = 600 − 336 = 264 cm²." - check: type: number q: "An L-shape fits exactly inside an 8 m by 6 m rectangle (one corner cut out). What is its perimeter in metres?" answer: 28 tolerance: 0 explain: "The steps in the L add up to the missing sides of the rectangle, so the perimeter is 8 + 6 + 8 + 6 = 28 m." - check: type: number q: "Review: what is the area of a triangle with base 6 cm and height 5 cm, in cm²?" answer: 15 tolerance: 0 explain: "½ × 6 × 5 = 15 cm²." - check: type: number q: "An L-shape is 10 m wide along the bottom and 7 m tall on the left. Its left part is 4 m wide; its right part is 6 m wide and only 3 m tall. What is its area in m²?" answer: 46 tolerance: 0 feedback: - ["70", "The right part is only 3 m tall: 6 × 3, not 6 × 7."] explain: "4 × 7 + 6 × 3 = 28 + 18 = 46 m²." smaller: check: { type: number, q: "Take the right part on its own: 6 m wide and 3 m tall. How many square metres is that part?", answer: 18, tolerance: 0, explain: "6 × 3 = 18 m². Now the left part, then add." } ``` ### Rectangle and triangle ### A frame ### Perimeter shortcut ### Review: triangles ### Another L ## Make: design a garden ```step stage: make insight: "Choosing two lengths to hit a target area uses the decomposition in reverse." try: { playground: board, starter: "shapes.yml#make", height: 600 } hint: ["The left part is always 3 × 6 = 18 m².", "The right part must be 38 − 18 = 20 m²."] check: { type: board, text: "Change a and b so the L-shaped garden has an area of 38 m².", when: "A = 38", explain: "18 + (a − 3) × b = 38, so (a − 3) × b = 20: a = 7 and b = 5, or a = 8 and b = 4." } ``` Then find your garden's perimeter, and say how many metres of edging it needs. ## Make: flooring and skirting, on paper ```step stage: make insight: "A living room that is a rectangle with a corner missing is quickest by taking away; flooring is an area and skirting is a perimeter, so they use different units." hint: ["Find the area of the whole 7 by 6 rectangle first.", "The missing corner is not floor. What do you do with its area?"] check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "A living room is an L-shape: 7 m along the bottom and 6 m up the left side, with a corner 4 m wide and 3 m deep missing from the top right. How many square metres of flooring cover it?" steps: - ["Whole rectangle: $7 \\times 6 = 42$ m²", "pretend the corner is there"] - ["Missing corner: $4 \\times 3 = 12$ m²", "this part is not floor"] - ["Floor: $42 - 12 = 30$ m²", "take the missing part away"] - ["Skirting board: $7 + 3 + 4 + 3 + 3 + 6 = 26$ m", "the perimeter adds every edge, in metres"] picks: - step: 3 q: "Why take 12 m² away from 42 m²?" options: - "The corner is inside the 7 by 6 rectangle but is not floor" - "The corner is more floor, so it should be added" - "You always take the smaller number from the bigger" answer: 0 feedback: [null, "The missing corner has no floor. Adding it would count floor that is not there.", "Which number is smaller is not the reason. Ask what the 12 m² is."] answer: "30" tolerance: 0 feedback: - ["42", "That is the whole rectangle, with the missing corner counted."] - ["54", "That adds the corner. It has no floor, so take it away."] - ["26", "That is the skirting, a length in metres. Flooring is an area."] criteria: - "I wrote the area of the whole rectangle and the area of the missing corner." - "I took the corner away, and my answer is in m²." - "I found the skirting as a perimeter in m, not m²." explain: "7 × 6 − 4 × 3 = 42 − 12 = 30 m² of flooring. Skirting goes round the edge: 26 m." ``` Do this one in your book, not on the screen. The room is made up for the task. A real job leaves out the doorways for the skirting and adds some for cutting waste. Write the big rectangle, take the corner away, and type the area. **Also used in** - **Building.** Flooring is sold by the square metre and skirting board by the metre. - **Houses.** The front of a house is a rectangle with a triangle for the roof, and paint is bought by the area. - **Maps.** A block of land with a corner cut off is a rectangle with a piece taken away. ```teacher summary: Students cut composite shapes into rectangles and triangles, or take pieces away from a rectangle, and find the area and the perimeter (AC9M8M01, node 1). time: 40 timing: Predict and Run 8 min · Investigate 10 min · Modify 10 min · Practise and Make 12 min goals: - I can cut a composite shape into pieces I know and add their areas. - I can find an area by taking pieces away from a big rectangle. - I can work out a missing side and the perimeter. struggle: Using each piece's own lengths. Ask students to write the two lengths on each piece before they multiply. before: > Do the Run board yourself first. Students need the area of rectangles and triangles (Area unit). The one idea: the area is the same however you cut it, as long as each piece uses its own lengths. The common mistake is giving a piece the whole shape's height (Ella's mistake). The board's three buttons cut across, cut up and down, or take away from the surrounding rectangle; it names each piece and gives its area. The perimeter needs every side, so missing sides (the ? sides) come first. Wider: floor plans of real rooms, shapes that need both adding and taking away. running: - "Predict: ask a 48 student what is missing from the rectangle." - "Run: ask which way they would choose for this shape, and why." - "Investigate: ask how tall each of Ella's pieces is." - "Modify: ask why taking away is quicker for the U." - "Make: ask for a second pair of lengths that also works." - "Paper: the L-shaped living room is worked in books; the page marks the flooring area and the reason for taking the corner away, then shows a model. Books out, and look for two areas written before the subtraction. Ask who also found the skirting." stuck: - see: A student uses the whole height for every piece. ask: How tall is this piece on its own? fix: Write each piece's two lengths on it before you multiply. - see: A student cannot find a missing side. ask: Which two sides together make the opposite side? fix: A missing side is the difference of two others. - see: A student gives a perimeter in m². ask: Are you counting squares or measuring a length? fix: "Perimeter is a length: m. Area counts squares: m²." stretch: Draw a floor plan of a room at home with at least six walls. Find its area two ways and its perimeter. support: Give the shape on grid paper so pieces can be counted as well as multiplied. leads: > This starts AC9M8M01. Where it leads: irregular shapes (next lesson), prisms with composite bases (Volume), and circles in composite shapes. exit: q: A rectangle 12 m by 5 m has a 4 m by 2 m corner cut out. Find its area. a: 12 × 5 − 4 × 2 = 60 − 8 = 52 m². explain: > A **composite shape** is made of shapes you know. **Cut** it into pieces and add their areas, or see a **big rectangle** and **take away** the missing pieces: both give the same area, if each piece uses its own lengths. Missing sides are differences of other sides. The **perimeter** adds every side, in units of length. ```

# Composite shapes for "Composite shapes". Corners go round the shape; letters are sliders.

# region: run
widget: composite
corners: 0,0; 8,0; 8,3; 3,3; 3,6; 0,6
split: on
units: m
# endregion

# region: explain
widget: composite
corners: 0,0; 8,0; 8,3; 3,3; 3,6; 0,6
split: on
units: m
# endregion

# region: explain-pic
widget: composite
corners: 0,0; 12,0; 12,9; 8,9; 8,4; 4,4; 4,9; 0,9
split: on
units: m
# endregion

# region: u-shape
widget: composite
corners: 0,0; 10,0; 10,8; 7,8; 7,3; 3,3; 3,8; 0,8
split: on
units: m
# endregion

# region: house
widget: composite
corners: 0,0; 8,0; 8,4; 4,7; 0,4
split: on
units: m
# endregion

# region: hidden
widget: composite
corners: 0,0; 8,0; 8,3; 3,3; 3,6; 0,6
hide: 3, 4
units: m
# endregion

# region: make
widget: composite
corners: 0,0; a,0; a,b; 3,b; 3,6; 0,6
slider a: 4, 10, 6
slider b: 1, 5, 2
split: on
units: m
# endregion
